newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - PHILIPS, LUCENT IN MAJOR COMMUNICATIONS DEAL.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - PHILIPS, LUCENT IN MAJOR COMMUNICATIONS DEAL.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV and Lucent Technologies Inc said on Tuesday they were planning to create a joint venture consumer communications company with an annual turnover of more than $2.5 billion.

The new company, to be called Philips Consumer Communications, would be the world leader in corded and cordless phones and answering machines, and would be generating an operating profit when the deal was finalised in October.
Head-quartered in New Jersey, it will have 12,400 employees, and will also manufacture and sell digital and analog cellular phones, pagers and other mobile electronic devices.
Philips will hold 60 percent of the joint venture and Lucent 40 percent.

Philips President Cor Boonstra said the group's consumer communications business was currently loss-making but that the new joint venture should be making a profit by October when the deal with Lucent was expected to be finalised.
"We...expect an operationally profitable business as of the first of October, 1997," the statement quoted him as saying.
Boonstra said that by joining up with the leading phones supplier in the U.S., Philips would accelerate its plans for growth in the core business of consumer communications.
The statement quoted Lucent Technologies President Rich McGinn as saying Lucent would benefit from Philips' global distribution capabilities and globally recognised brand name.
Mike McTighe, currently managing director of the Philips consumer communications division, will be chief executive officer of the new company.
Dutch share analysts welcomed the deal, saying it gave Philips the mass it needed to slug it out with the top three in telecommunications hardware, Motorola , Nokia of Finland and Ericsson of Sweden.

"Lucent is a big player in the U.S. and in a strong position in all kinds of phones production. Philips has much more focus on wireless -- if you put the two together you've got a very big player," said Eric de Graaf of ING Barings.
"The key reason for this is getting a bigger firm to make it possible to expand in this fast moving business," he said.

"The joint venture is number four in global telephone markets, behind Motorola, Nokia and Ericsson, and it's going to be number one in fixed line and cordless phones and answering machines, although that's not the fast growing market that everyone's aiming at," added De Graaf.
Analysts said they had been impressed at the speed with which Philips had carved out the Lucent deal.

Philips' consumer communications business began operations in January 1996 and had been booking start-up losses as it struggled to gain a foothold for its products in the mobile phone, cordless phone, pager and answering machine markets.

"All in all it gives Philips a good opportunity. Up until now we thought Philips was too small in this (telecoms) market and would never get big enough to engage the competition like Nokia, Ericsson and Motorola," said Wortel.
Before the deal he estimated Philips was at the lower end of the top 10 of the communications equipment market.

"Now they have the deal with Lucent it means they'll be pretty big, number four or five perhaps at the end of this year, which means that if they grow further, especially in the U.S, they might go into the top three. That's what Philips has to do to make this worthwhile and make money on the deal," he said.
De Graaf said it was a move that signalled Philips was working hard to become a key player the market.

"They've said that they didn't want to do everything on their own like they have with a number of products that failed. Now they're spreading their risks and of course their rewards, but it's a means to grow faster because you have to have a certain size in this market," he said.

Philips shares soared 7.90 guilders to a record high close of 128.90 guilders in a mostly lower Amsterdam bourse. Analysts said the shares had been boosted by the Lucent venture news as well as a positive presentation in Eindhoven from Philips about its Sound & Vision unit's performance. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
